tagline: Along Bayou Boeuf, after Solomon Northup's twelve years.
intro: The trail runs 83 miles from Alexandria down the Bayou Boeuf country to Marksville, with 22 signs to mark the stops. It follows Solomon Northup, a free-born farmer and violinist from New York who went to Washington in 1841 for a job as a traveling musician and was kidnapped there and sold. He came off the steamer Rodolf at the Red River landing in Alexandria under the name Platt.
He was held on the plantations of this valley until 1853. Back in New York he wrote Twelve Years a Slave, and the film made of it won the Oscar for Best Picture.

moments.title: Epps House
moments.text: At the Epps House, now on the campus of LSU at Alexandria, Northup met and confided in Samuel Bass, a Canadian-born carpenter whose letters north at last got word to his family.

moments.title: Cheneyville
moments.text: William Prince Ford, Northup's first enslaver, led most of his Baptist congregation here into the Church of Christ in 1843, and in 1857 Alexander Campbell admired its fellowship between the races.

moments.title: Marksville
moments.text: In 1853 a New York lawyer, a local attorney and the sheriff went out to the Epps plantation on Bayou Boeuf, and at the parish courthouse here the papers making Northup free were signed.
